Cleaning fossil records

Source: vignettes/fossils.Rmd
fossils.Rmd

Fossil occurrences, such as those downloaded from the Paleobiology Database (PBDB), can carry the same coordinate errors as modern records, and they have one more field to check: the age of the record, given as a range in million years (Ma). This article flags a small fossil table with the coordinate tests and the age test age_equal, filters records by the width of their age range, tests a larger table for outliers within a taxon, and exports the kept records to PyRate. Get started covers installation; the comparison with CoordinateCleaner at the end also needs that package installed.

  1. Flag a fossil table with flag_occurrences().

  2. Filter out flagged records, using keep_unflagged().

  3. Filter by the width of the age range, counting each group with tally_flags().

  4. Test each taxon for outliers in age and space.

  5. Export the kept records with export_pyrate().

A small fossil table

PBDB uses accepted_name for taxon names, lng and lat for coordinates, and cc for two-letter country codes. The columns min_ma and max_ma give the youngest and oldest possible ages in millions of years before the present.

The example below contains nine synthetic records, each built for one case; the cases are explained beside the flags they produce. Records 1 and 9 are the controls: a minimum age below the maximum age, a span under 4 million years, and coordinates in Wyoming that match their country code US. Records 7 and 8 have the country code DE; their coordinates are missing in the table and set in the next chunk:

library(OccurrenceCleaner)

fos <- data.frame(
  occurrence_no = 1:9,
  accepted_name = c("Coryphodon", "Coryphodon", "Hyracotherium", "Hyracotherium",
                    "Hyracotherium", "Mesonyx", "Mesonyx", "Mesonyx", "Uintatherium"),
  lng = c(-108.52, -108.40, -108.71, -107.95, -108.10, 0, NA, NA, -109.03),
  lat = c(44.31, 44.05, 43.92, 44.60, 44.40, 0, NA, NA, 41.62),
  cc = c("US", "US", "US", "US", "US", "US", "DE", "DE", "US"),
  min_ma = c(53.0, 55.8, 56.0, 23.0, NA, 48.6, 47.8, 47.8, 46.2),
  max_ma = c(56.0, 55.8, 52.5, 66.0, 54.0, 50.2, 49.0, 49.0, 48.6))

Records 7 and 8 are placed relative to the centroid of Germany in the package’s reference points, so their distance to it is known: record 7 sits on the point, record 8 lies 0.027 degrees of latitude (about 3 km) north of it. Their ages are ordered, with a span of 1.2 million years.

cen <- reference_points("centroid")
de <- cen[cen$key == "ne:DEU" & cen$method == "polygon centroid", ]
de[, c("name", "method", "lon", "lat")]
#>        name           method      lon      lat
#> 380 Germany polygon centroid 10.36071 51.05001
fos[7:8, "lng"] <- de$lon
fos[7:8, "lat"] <- de$lat + c(0, 0.027)

Flagging

occ_columns() maps the PBDB names onto the fields the tests read. The coordinate tests are the record tests of clean_fossils() in CoordinateCleaner; age_equal is its agesequal test, and the country check runs too because the table has country codes:

cols <- occ_columns(lon = "lng", lat = "lat", species = "accepted_name",
                    country = "cc", id = "occurrence_no")
tests <- c("invalid", "zero", "equal", "centroid", "institution",
           "gbif_headquarters", "country_mismatch", "age_equal")
f <- flag_occurrences(fos, tests = tests, columns = cols)
f[, c("occurrence_no", "accepted_name", "min_ma", "max_ma", "flags")]
#> <occ_flags> 9 records, 8 tests, reference OccurrenceCleaner 0.2.0, land 110
#>   occurrence_no accepted_name min_ma max_ma  flags                  flagged_by
#> 1             1    Coryphodon   53.0   56.0      0                            
#> 2             2    Coryphodon   55.8   55.8 524288                   age_equal
#> 3             3 Hyracotherium   56.0   52.5 524288                   age_equal
#> 4             4 Hyracotherium   23.0   66.0      0                            
#> 5             5 Hyracotherium     NA   54.0      0                            
#> 6             6       Mesonyx   48.6   50.2    518 zero,equal,country_mismatch
#> 7             7       Mesonyx   47.8   49.0     16                    centroid
#> 8             8       Mesonyx   47.8   49.0      0                            
#> 9             9  Uintatherium   46.2   48.6      0

age_equal flags a record whose minimum age is equal to or greater than its maximum age. Record 2 has equal minimum and maximum ages and record 3 has them reversed, so both are flagged. A zero-width range can come from one age copied into both fields, and an inverted one from swapped fields, but the flag only records the comparison; such records need a look at their source before they are corrected or dropped. Record 5 is missing its minimum age, so this test cannot compare its ages and leaves it unflagged. Record 4 spans 43 million years; no test flags a wide range on its own, and the section on filtering by age range comes back to it.

Record 6 has both coordinates set to zero and fails zero, equal and country_mismatch, since (0, 0) lies in the Gulf of Guinea. Record 7 fails centroid: it lies within the default 1 km of the centroid of Germany. Record 8, 3 km from it, passes.

Filtering records

keep_unflagged() keeps the records that no test in tests flags. It also checks that every named test was run on the flagged table, and stops with an error if one was not. The later sections reuse this rule as rule:

rule <- tests
kept <- keep_unflagged(f, rule)
kept[, c("occurrence_no", "accepted_name", "min_ma", "max_ma")]
#>   occurrence_no accepted_name min_ma max_ma
#> 1             1    Coryphodon   53.0   56.0
#> 4             4 Hyracotherium   23.0   66.0
#> 5             5 Hyracotherium     NA   54.0
#> 8             8       Mesonyx   47.8   49.0
#> 9             9  Uintatherium   46.2   48.6

Record 5 stays because age_equal cannot compare a missing age, so the record carries no flag. A study that needs both ages adds !is.na(f$min_ma) & !is.na(f$max_ma) to the selection.

A wider centroid buffer

OccurrenceCleaner uses default buffers of 1 km around centroids and 100 m around institutions. You can change these with buffers.

Fossil localities can be georeferenced coarsely, so a collection placed a few kilometres from a country centroid may have been assigned the country-centroid coordinates. A wider buffer catches such records, at the cost of flagging any correct locality within the same distance. With a 5 km buffer, chosen here to reach record 8, both records near the centroid of Germany are flagged:

f5 <- flag_occurrences(fos, tests = tests, columns = cols,
                       buffers = list(centroid = 5000))
data.frame(occurrence_no = fos$occurrence_no,
           centroid_1km = f$flag_centroid, centroid_5km = f5$flag_centroid)
#>   occurrence_no centroid_1km centroid_5km
#> 1             1        FALSE        FALSE
#> 2             2        FALSE        FALSE
#> 3             3        FALSE        FALSE
#> 4             4        FALSE        FALSE
#> 5             5        FALSE        FALSE
#> 6             6        FALSE        FALSE
#> 7             7         TRUE         TRUE
#> 8             8        FALSE         TRUE
#> 9             9        FALSE        FALSE

These defaults differ from those in CoordinateCleaner. In version 3.0.1, clean_fossils() applies its defaults centroids_rad = 0.05 and inst_rad = 0.001 as radii in metres, so its centroid and institution tests flag only records within 5 cm and 1 mm of a reference point.

Filtering by age range

Calculate the width of each record’s age range as max_ma - min_ma. Use tally_flags() to count flagged and retained records in each age-range group:

f$age_range <- f$max_ma - f$min_ma
tally_flags(f, bins = list(age_range = c(5, 15)), rules = list(all = rule))
#> <occ_tally> 9 records in 3 groups of age_range_bin, rules: all
#>  age_range_bin n removed_all kept_all
#>             <5 7           4        3
#>           >=15 1           0        1
#>        missing 1           0        1
#> # summary() for the share each test flags

Record 4 has an age range of 43 Ma and is the only record above 15 Ma. To retain unflagged records with an age range of at most 15 Ma, apply the limit to the kept records; which() also drops records without an age range:

kept15 <- keep_unflagged(f, rule)
kept15 <- kept15[which(kept15$age_range <= 15), ]
kept15$occurrence_no
#> [1] 1 8 9

The 15 Ma limit is illustrative; choose a limit appropriate for your study. You can change it without rerunning the flagging tests.

For comparison, CoordinateCleaner provides this filter through cf_range() with method = "time", which flags age ranges wider than max_range Ma.

Outliers within a taxon

Three tests compare each record with others in the same taxon. Here, taxa are the genera in accepted_name:

  • age_range_outlier identifies unusually wide age ranges.

  • age_outlier identifies unusual ages.

  • spatiotemporal_outlier identifies unusual combinations of location and age.

The tests use an upper threshold calculated within each taxon: the 75th percentile plus mltpl times the interquartile range, with mltpl = 5 by default. Each test applies this threshold to its own measure of difference. Taxa need at least seven records to be tested.

The two tests that use ages, age_outlier and spatiotemporal_outlier, sample one age from each record’s range. They repeat this five times and flag records identified in a majority of runs. Sampling uses a seed for each taxon, making the results reproducible. You can change the seed through settings.

Generate 600 synthetic records with PBDB column names. Locations fall within a region of Wyoming, ages span 46 to 60 Ma, and age ranges are 1 to 4 Ma wide. Genera are assigned independently of location and age.

Then give 20 records a broad age range of 23 to 66 Ma and five records an age range of 99 to 101 Ma. The injected_case column labels these changes; unchanged records are labelled background.

set.seed(5)
n <- 600
big <- data.frame(
  occurrence_no = 100 + seq_len(n),
  accepted_name = sample(c("Coryphodon", "Hyracotherium", "Mesonyx"), n, TRUE),
  lng = round(runif(n, -110, -106), 3), lat = round(runif(n, 42, 46), 3),
  cc = "US", min_ma = round(runif(n, 46, 56), 1), injected_case = "background")
big$max_ma <- big$min_ma + round(runif(n, 1, 4), 1)
i <- sample(n, 25)
big[i[1:20], c("min_ma", "max_ma", "injected_case")] <- list(23, 66, "broad_range")
big[i[21:25], c("min_ma", "max_ma", "injected_case")] <- list(99, 101, "far_age")
table(big$injected_case)
#> 
#>  background broad_range     far_age 
#>         575          20           5

Run the outlier tests alongside the coordinate and age tests to collect their flags in one table:

otests <- c("age_range_outlier", "age_outlier", "spatiotemporal_outlier")
g <- flag_occurrences(big, tests = c(tests, otests), columns = cols)
aggregate(as.data.frame(g)[paste0("flag_", otests)],
          by = list(injected_case = g$injected_case), FUN = sum)
#>   injected_case flag_age_range_outlier flag_age_outlier
#> 1    background                      0                0
#> 2   broad_range                     20                7
#> 3       far_age                      0                5
#>   flag_spatiotemporal_outlier
#> 1                           0
#> 2                           0
#> 3                           4

The range test flags all 20 broad-range records. The age test flags seven broad-range records and all five records near 100 Ma. The spatiotemporal test flags four of the five records near 100 Ma. All three tests leave the background records unflagged.

You can adjust the tests through settings. The call below lowers mltpl to 2 for the range test and changes the age test’s seed to 7:

g2 <- flag_occurrences(big, tests = otests, columns = cols,
                       settings = list(age_range_outlier = list(mltpl = 2),
                                       age_outlier = list(seed = 7)))
colSums(as.data.frame(g2)[paste0("flag_", otests)])
#>      flag_age_range_outlier            flag_age_outlier 
#>                          20                          14 
#> flag_spatiotemporal_outlier 
#>                           4

The range test still flags the same 20 records: their 43 Ma ranges exceed the threshold under both settings. Changing the age test’s seed gives 14 flagged records, compared with 12 under the default seed.

Export to PyRate

PyRate (Silvestro et al. 2014) estimates speciation and extinction rates from fossil occurrences. Select the records from g that are not flagged by any of the tests run and have an age range of at most 15 Ma:

g$age_range <- g$max_ma - g$min_ma
final <- keep_unflagged(g)
final <- final[which(final$age_range <= 15), ]
nrow(final)
#> [1] 575

export_pyrate() writes them in PyRate’s input format: one array of ages per taxon, an extra age of 0 for extant taxa, and replicates of ages drawn from each record’s range.

paths <- export_pyrate(final, file.path(tempdir(), "wyoming"), status = "extinct",
                       columns = cols, replicates = 3, seed = 1)
basename(paths)
#> [1] "wyoming_PyRate.py"     "wyoming_TaxonList.txt"

The _PyRate.py file contains the ages and is the input PyRate reads; the _TaxonList.txt file lists each taxon with its status. The draws are seeded, so the same call writes the same files; random = FALSE uses the midpoints of the ranges instead. CoordinateCleaner’s write_pyrate() writes the same layout, and the package tests compare the two files.

Comparison with CoordinateCleaner

age_equal and cf_equal() give the same flags on the small table:

theirs <- !CoordinateCleaner::cf_equal(fos, value = "flagged", verbose = FALSE)
data.frame(occurrence_no = fos$occurrence_no,
           OccurrenceCleaner = f$flag_age_equal, CoordinateCleaner = theirs)
#>   occurrence_no OccurrenceCleaner CoordinateCleaner
#> 1             1             FALSE             FALSE
#> 2             2              TRUE              TRUE
#> 3             3              TRUE              TRUE
#> 4             4             FALSE             FALSE
#> 5             5             FALSE             FALSE
#> 6             6             FALSE             FALSE
#> 7             7             FALSE             FALSE
#> 8             8             FALSE             FALSE
#> 9             9             FALSE             FALSE

The package’s test suite compares the outlier tests with cf_age(), cf_outl() and cf_range(): age_range_outlier gives identical flags, and the two tests that draw ages give identical flags when no age has to be drawn.

Fossils in GBIF data

GBIF stores fossil specimens alongside modern records, marked by basisOfRecord = "FOSSIL_SPECIMEN", usually without PBDB-style age fields. basis_fossil flags them:

gb <- data.frame(
  gbifID = 1:3,
  basisOfRecord = c("HUMAN_OBSERVATION", "FOSSIL_SPECIMEN", "PRESERVED_SPECIMEN"),
  decimalLongitude = c(16.37, 11.2, 14.5), decimalLatitude = c(48.21, 50.1, 47.1))
fg <- flag_occurrences(gb, tests = c("invalid", "basis_fossil"))

A study of present-day distributions keeps the records without the flag, and a palaeontological one keeps only the flagged records:

keep_unflagged(fg, "basis_fossil")[, c("gbifID", "basisOfRecord")]
#>   gbifID      basisOfRecord
#> 1      1  HUMAN_OBSERVATION
#> 3      3 PRESERVED_SPECIMEN
fg[has_flag(fg, "basis_fossil"), c("gbifID", "basisOfRecord")]
#>   gbifID   basisOfRecord
#> 2      2 FOSSIL_SPECIMEN

References

Silvestro, D., Schnitzler, J., Liow, L. H., Antonelli, A. and Salamin, N. (2014). Bayesian estimation of speciation and extinction from incomplete fossil occurrence data. Systematic Biology 63:349-367. https://doi.org/10.1093/sysbio/syu006
